title: Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham both included in Real Madrid squad for Manchester City game
content:
Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham have been included in the travelling squad for the team’s Champions League last 16 second leg against Manchester City on Tuesday.

Mbappe has been dealing with discomfort in his left knee since early December and has not played since February 21, while Bellingham has been absent with a hamstring injury since February 1.

It is not a guarantee that both will be included in the matchday squad, though Champions League regulations allow teams to name up to 12 players on the bench. Mbappe is more likely to receive minutes if he continues to progress in Monday’s training session.

Madrid enter the second leg in Manchester with a 3-0 aggregate advantage after a Federico Valverde hat-trick at the Bernabeu on Wednesday.

Mbappe, who trained with the group last week, had played through the knee issue, frequently scoring goals before his most recent spell on the sidelines. The Athletic reported that there have been fears of aggravating the injury if he was to return to action prematurely, according to sources briefed on the situation.

Madrid have described the injury as a knee sprain, with head coach Alvaro Arbeloa saying last month that the club “decided that he should stop, recover, and come back with confidence”.

The 27-year-old travelled to Paris at the start of this month for additional tests on the issue. The player’s camp told The Athletic that it was a step taken “in agreement with the club” though “surgery is not being considered”.

Mbappe has been in prolific form for Madrid this season, scoring 38 goals in 33 games in all competitions.

Meanwhile, Bellingham, 22, went to London to see a specialist about his hamstring injury. Both visits were conducted alongside members of Madrid’s medical department.

The England international sustained the issue in a 2-1 win over Rayo Vallecano. He was initially expected to return in early March, though The Athletic reported that the injury is more complex than suggested by the club at first, with his timeline for recovery updated to six to eight weeks. Sources said that the club were hopeful that he could return for the second leg against City.

Bellingham has scored six goals and proved four assists in 28 games in all competitions for Madrid this season.

Defenders Alvaro Carreras and David Alaba have also been included in the squad after missing the first leg, though Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio have not travelled. Dani Ceballos is sidelined with a calf injury picked up in February, while the Brazilian pair of Eder Militao and Rodrygo remain out with longer-term injuries.
